explanation: Real-world problems like a tossed ball turn into quadratics because gravity makes height a parabola in time. Here h(t) = -1/2 g t^2 + v0 t + h0 maps time on the x-axis to height on the y-axis, and a dot rides the arc on a loop. The vertex (violet) is the PEAK height and the time it occurs is v0/g, while the green dot is where the object lands (h = 0). Slide the launch speed v0, starting height h0, and gravity g to see how the peak rises and the landing time shifts -- the same algebra behind 'how high' and 'when does it hit the ground' questions.
bullets: Constant gravity makes height a downward parabola in time t.
The vertex t = v0/g gives the maximum height; it is the axis of symmetry.
The positive root of h(t) = 0 is the landing time -- solve with the quadratic formula.
